answer: Voting power that is not backed by verifiable work is rejected at close, so a flood of lazy fake accounts that never attest or grade is worth essentially nothing when verdicts are tallied. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. This design turns the attacker's greatest weapon — scale — into its weakest point, because scale is exactly what becomes unaffordable to maintain. Consider a spiral as the anchor of the cost.
